newsitem.title: USA: CME live and feeder cattle calls range mixed.
newsitem.headline: CME live and feeder cattle calls range mixed.

text.p: Early calls on CME live cattle futures ranged mixed, from 0.200 cent per lb higher to 0.200 lower while feeder cattle calls ranged from 0.100 cent higher to 0.100 lower, livestock analysts said.

Analysts looked for strength in the spot June live cattle contract on this week's strong tone to cash markets. Packers paid $64 per cwt for fed cattle on Tuesday, $1.00 higher than last significant trade, and expectations are for prices to reach $65, possibly this week. A jump in boxed beef values to two week highs were also cited.
Boxed beef rose $2.73 to $1.53 per cwt with heavyweight choice up to $102.47, the highest since June 3.

However, deferred months were again expected to show resistance on expectations of declining prices once supermarket chains finish buying wholesale beef for the Independence Day holiday. The trend is for beef and fed cattle prices to move lower into the summer. This could be especially evident in light of the large number of cattle on feed and increased number of contracted cattle that packers have available in July, they said.
Feeder cattle could show strength on an increase in the CME feeder cattle index, but higher corn futures indications and technical weakness could weigh on the market, they said.
The market looked technically disappointing after failing to post new contract highs Tuesday and weakening to end mixed on the day, they added.
The latest CME feeder cattle index advanced $0.14 to $77.60 per cwt.
